en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Sixteenth Chapter
The Discussion on Grasping with Attention: Does one attend by grasping?
Yes, [one does].
“Does one know that mind by means of that same mind?
“One should not say so.
…pe… “Does one know that mind by means of that same mind?”
“Yes,” [you say].
“Does that consciousness know that consciousness as ‘consciousness’?
One should not say so … [and so on] …
Does one understand that mind as “mind” by means of that [other] mind?
Yes. Is that mind the object of that [other] mind?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is that consciousness the object of that consciousness? Yes.
By means of that contact, one contacts that contact; by means of that feeling … [and so on] … by means of that perception … by means of that volition …
by that mind … by that applied thought … by that sustained thought …
Does one understand that wisdom by means of that rapture, by means of that mindfulness, and by means of that wisdom?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … When one attends to the past as “past,” does one attend to the future as “future”?
It should not be said thus … [as before].
If one attends to the past as “past,” does one attend to the future as “future”?
Yes. [Does this apply] to two types of contact? ...pe... [and so on].
“Do two states of consciousness coincide?
One should not say so… [etc.
…When one attends to the past as “past,” does one attend to the present as “present”?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … When one attends to the past as “past,” does one attend to the present as “present”? Yes.
Is there a convergence of two contacts …pe… of two consciousnesses?
One should certainly not say so …pe….
When one attends to the past as "past," does one attend to the future as "future" and attend to the present as "present"?
One should not say so... [etc.
... When one attends to the past as "past," does one attend to the future as "future" and attend to the present as "present"?
“Yes,” he said.
“Are there then a convergence of three types of contact … pe … and a convergence of three types of consciousness?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … When one attends to the future as "future," does one attend to the past as "past"?
It should not be said thus … [as before] …
When one attends to the future as "future," does one attend to the past as "past"?
Yes. [Does this apply to] two types of contact... and so forth.
“Do two states of consciousness coincide?
One should not say so… [and so on]… When one attends to the future as “future,” does one attend to the present as “present”?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … When one attends to the future as “future,” does one attend to the present as “present”? Yes.
Is there a conjunction of two contacts …pe… of two consciousnesses?
One should not say so …pe….
When one attends to the future as "future," does one attend to the past as "past" and the present as "present"?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
When one attends to the future as "future," does one attend to the past as "past" and the present as "present"?
“Yes,” he said.
“Is there a convergence of three types of contact … pe … and three types of consciousness?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … When one attends to the present as “present,” does one attend to the past as “past”?
It should not be said thus … [as before] …
When one attends to the present as "present," does one attend to the past as "past"?
Yes. [Does this apply] to two types of contact? ...pe... [and so on].
“Do two states of consciousness coincide?
One should not say so… [and so on]… When one attends to the present as “present,” does one attend to the future as “future”?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … When one attends to the present as "present," does one attend to the future as "future"? Yes.
"Is there a convergence of two contacts... [and so on] ...of two consciousnesses?
One should not say this... [and so on].
When one attends to the present as "present," does one attend to the past as "past" and the future as "future"?
One should not say so... [etc.
... When one attends to the present as "present," does one attend to the past as "past" and the future as "future"?
“Yes,” he said.
“Then do the three types of contact … [and so on] … the three types of consciousness coincide?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Should it not be said:
“Having attained, one attends to it”?
“Yes. [The opponent asks: “Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
‘All conditioned phenomena are impermanent’?”
When one sees with wisdom,
then one becomes disenchanted with suffering;
this is the path to purification.
When one sees with wisdom that "all conditioned phenomena are suffering," then one becomes disenchanted with suffering.
This is the path to purification:
when one sees with wisdom that all phenomena are non-self.
“Then one becomes disenchanted with suffering;
this is the path to purification.
Is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes.
“In that case, one attends by having grasped [the object].
The discussion on attending by having grasped is finished.
